/* player.css — DERIVED FROM styles.css. Do not edit by hand.

   A strict subset: every block whose selectors a player page can match, in
   their ORIGINAL relative order, plus every at-rule that cannot be classified
   by matching (@keyframes, @font-face) and every media query the harness does
   not enter (print, reduced-motion, orientation). Those are held regardless of
   whether they matched — the classifier may ship a rule the player does not
   need and may not drop one it does.

   WHY A SUBSET AND NOT A SPLIT. The obvious shape — a shared base plus an
   editor overlay — was built, and its screenshots failed. Kept and editor-only
   blocks interleave through styles.css 113 and 530 times respectively, so
   NEITHER load order reproduces the original cascade and seven of eleven editor
   scenes rendered differently. A subset changes no editor at all: styles.css is
   untouched and both editors still load the whole of it.

   THE COST IS DUPLICATION, and it is paid for by an assertion rather than by
   discipline. verify_cssplit.py regenerates this file with
   harness/tools/cssgraph.py and fails if the result differs by one byte, so a
   rule edited in styles.css and not regenerated here is a red suite, not a
   silent divergence. Regenerate; never hand-sort.

   Generated by harness/tools/cssgraph.py --emit. */
